chart_references: Alas, these days the giant is sleepy. The bloc’s GDP and its stockmarket have lagged far behind America’s over the past decade (see charts 1 and 2). In April activity in its services sector fell to a 62-month low. The recent shocks which contributed to the sluggishness were not of its own making: the covid-19 pandemic, Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and now America’s war on Iran. But the EU and its members have also been getting in their own way, by overregulating companies (see chart 3) and failing to properly integrate their supposedly single market.

extraction.title: Simplify and integrate
extraction.subtitle: The EU wants to unshackle its economy. For real this time Eurocrats are belatedly developing a healthy distaste for red tape
extraction.summary: The EU is confronting a decade of sluggish growth by slashing bureaucracy and deepening market integration. New “omnibus” bills aim to cut firms’ reporting costs by €37.5 bn by 2029, while proposals such as services passports and a “28th regime” for pan‑European startups target a 3 % GDP boost over ten years. Political backing from von der Leyen and the finance commissioner is strong, but national resistance and recent negotiation breakdowns threaten implementation.
